subject: redPanda
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: red panda balancing on a mossy stone.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
Looking at the render, the panda's pose and dark coloring mostly work, but the scarf reads oddly as a flat octagonal collar plate rather than a soft wrapped scarf, so that's something I need to fix.

Also the ribbon tails stick up like antennae instead of draping down the back — I need to lower the curve's rise and widen the spread so the ribbons hug the back and fall over the flanks naturally instead of floating above the body.

I'm also reconsidering the collar shape — the octagon-looking teal frame with gold trim is probably just the body loft's wide neck section at that z-depth, not a separate collar loop, so I should check whether the neck width there is actually causing that chest-plate look.

Separately, the proportions feel off: the head sits too low and small while the neck and body look too long and weasel-like for a red panda, so I'm considering scaling up the head skull parts to make it chunkier, though that would require touching many individual pieces.

For the legs, the front columns look fine and the paw-to-stone contact seems reasonable, but the moss blobs scattered on the stone rim are oversized, looking like broccoli clusters that clutter the top of the stone and block the view.

For the Vision gem, it's attached via a hanging belt strap on the flank with a gold-framed setting, positioned near [0.3, 0.57, -0.02]; the brown octagonal belt loop is visible beside the leg in the three-quarter view since the body shape is boxy, which is acceptable but not ideal.

The tail is nice but stiff, with jagged dark orange spiky tufts and a dark plum tip cap, alternating rings, and a decent upward curve though the tuft cards look a bit sparse. The glow leaf cards and loose octahedra float nicely. Eyes and cream ear interiors look good, forehead tufts resemble curled orange horn-like spirals between the ears which is fine, and the cheek ruff blades read as pale spiky wings that work well for red panda cheeks.

Now I'm checking the platform, which is huge relative to the panda — the subject reads too small in frame since the platform radius dominates the overall width compared to the panda's length including tail, so I should consider reducing it. I'm also thinking the pose reads more as walking on all fours than actually balancing, so lifting a front paw with a bent elbow would sell the "balancing on a mossy stone" concept better — I'm working out the IK targets and limb lengths to raise that foreleg convincingly.

For implementing the raised paw, I need to swap the hardcoded foot height for a dynamic target so the paw actually tracks the lifted position, and adjust the paw's forward placement slightly. I'm weighing the risk since the front leg's three-point chain (root, elbow, end) needs to stay consistent when one leg's proportions shift.

I'm also tuning the belly shading (lightening the dark plum a bit so legs don't go too black), shrinking the moss blob sizes, and reconsidering the ribbon spike placement so they still land naturally at the flank with the new leg routing -- keeping these as a small batch of targeted edits rather than a big overhaul.

For the leg geometry, I'm modifying the foot limb code so that one side gets a raised foot position when needed, computing a lifted foot point and reusing the same limb curve logic, then double-checking the reach from root to foot still stays within range.

Now I'm updating the paw placement code to reference the new lifted foot variable instead of the hardcoded FOOT value across each of the paw sections.

Still adjusting ribbon placement and spike direction...

Lightening the dark color to a richer magenta tone, #5e3548, to finish up.
